topics.topic: The Colonial Administrative System: Indirect Rule in Northern Nigeria (Emirates and Native Authority)
learningObjectives: Define Indirect Rule as the British system of governance through pre-existing indigenous political institutions
Analyze why Indirect Rule succeeded brilliantly in Northern Nigeria (hierarchical emirate structure, Islamic taxation, obedient subjects)
Examine the tripartite institutional structure: British Resident, Native Authority (Emir), and Native Courts/Treasury

topics.topic: The Colonial Administrative System: Indirect Rule in Western Nigeria and Eastern Nigeria
learningObjectives: Analyze the partial success of Indirect Rule in Western Nigeria: tensions arising from enhancing royal powers over traditional checks and balances
Examine the catastrophic failure of Indirect Rule in Eastern Nigeria due to decentralized republican tradition and arbitrary appointment of 'Warrant Chiefs'
Analyze the Aba Women’s Riot of 1929: causes, anti-taxation uprising, destruction of Native Courts, and historical significance

topics.topic: Colonial Economic Policies: Cash crop production, railway infrastructure, and mineral extraction
learningObjectives: Explain the deliberate colonial focus on cash crops for metropolitan export (groundnut pyramids in Kano, cocoa in West, palm oil in East)
Trace railway construction (Lagos-Kano, Port Harcourt-Enugu) designed to evacuate minerals and agricultural produce to coastal ports
Examine colonial taxation, monetization, forced labor schemes, and the marginalization of indigenous industrialization

topics.topic: Early Nationalist Movements in Nigeria (1914-1939): Herbert Macaulay, NNDP, and NYM
learningObjectives: Trace the birth of modern Nigerian nationalism led by educated Lagos elites protesting water rates and racial segregation
Examine the leadership of Herbert Macaulay ('Father of Nigerian Nationalism') and the Nigerian National Democratic Party (NNDP)
Analyze the founding of the Nigerian Youth Movement (NYM) in 1934 by Ernest Ikoli, Dr. J.C. Vaughan, and H.O. Davies

topics.topic: Impact of World War II on Nigerian Nationalism: The Atlantic Charter and radical trade unionism
learningObjectives: Analyze the return of Nigerian soldiers (ex-servicemen) from Burma and Europe and the demystification of the 'white man'
Examine the inspirational effect of the 1941 Atlantic Charter affirming the right of all peoples to self-determination
Trace Michael Imoudu’s leadership in the 1945 General Strike paralyzing the colonial economy for 44 days

topics.topic: Militant Nationalism and Post-War Political Parties: NCNC, Zikist Movement, Action Group, and NPC
learningObjectives: Analyze the founding of the National Council of Nigeria and the Cameroons (NCNC) led by Herbert Macaulay and Dr. Nnamdi Azikiwe
Examine the revolutionary civil disobedience campaigns and strikes of the Zikist Movement (Rajih Abdallah, Osita Agwuna)
Trace the establishment of the Action Group (AG) under Chief Obafemi Awolowo and the Northern People's Congress (NPC) under Sir Ahmadu Bello

topics.topic: Mid-Term Continuous Assessment & Constitutional Development Clinic
learningObjectives: Assess pupil mastery of Indirect Rule, early nationalism, and post-war party formations
Conduct a debate on 'The Aba Women's War of 1929 as the Pre-eminent Anti-Colonial Uprising in Nigeria'
Provide remedial instruction on distinguishing between early and radical post-WWII nationalism

topics.topic: Constitutional Road to Independence: Clifford (1922), Richards (1946), and Macpherson (1951) Constitutions
learningObjectives: Examine the 1922 Clifford Constitution introducing the elective principle and establishing the Legislative Council
Analyze the 1946 Richards Constitution creating Regional Houses of Assembly and institutionalizing regionalism
Examine the 1951 Macpherson Constitution resulting from nationwide village, district, and regional consultative conferences

topics.topic: Constitutional Road to Independence: Lyttelton (1954) Constitution and the Federal System
learningObjectives: Detail the historic 1953 Kano Riots and Anthony Enahoro's Motion for Self-Government in 1956
Analyze the landmark 1954 Lyttelton Constitution formalizing true federalism, regional autonomy, and civil services
Trace the attainment of Regional Self-Government by the Eastern and Western Regions (1957) and Northern Region (1959)

topics.topic: The Willink Commission (1957-1958) and Minority Fears in the Three Regions
learningObjectives: Analyze the fears of ethnic minorities regarding dominant majorities in the Northern, Western, and Eastern regions
Examine the recommendations of the Sir Henry Willink Commission rejecting new states but proposing a Bill of Rights
Evaluate the insertion of Chapter III Fundamental Human Rights in the 1960 Independence Constitution

topics.topic: The 1959 Federal Elections and Attainment of National Independence (October 1, 1960)
learningObjectives: Analyze the multi-party campaigning and results of the historic December 1959 pre-independence federal elections
Examine the parliamentary coalition government formed between the NPC and NCNC with Sir Abubakar Tafawa Balewa as Prime Minister
Detail the lowering of the British Union Jack, hoisting of the Green-White-Green flag, and celebrations on October 1, 1960

topics.topic: Comprehensive WASSCE/NECO History Revision & Past Question Marathon
learningObjectives: Review the entire 3-year senior secondary Nigerian history curriculum from ancient Nok culture to 1960 independence
Execute timed speed drills on 50 objective questions and construct 4 detailed analytical essays
Perfect historical chronology, cause-and-effect arguments, and primary source citations in examination essays

topics.topic: Terminal Mock Examination and Broadsheet Entry
learningObjectives: Administer comprehensive mock WASSCE History examination under official testing standards
Grade answers strictly according to West African Examination Council marking schemes
Certify final continuous assessment grades for official graduation records and academic transcripts
